_meta.name: Absolute clinical reference limits per measurement
_meta.purpose: Independent safety net beside NEWS2. NEWS2 scores acute deterioration; these limits flag values that are clinically abnormal on their own, even without history, without a personal baseline, or when a pathological baseline collapses (e.g. a collapsed band from several identical high readings).
_meta.generatedBy: Researched from public clinical sources with AI assistance (OpenCode). Must be checked by a human against the cited sources before use.
_meta.notes: Adult (18+) limits, sex-independent. Pregnancy is excluded (see NEWS2 limits). Each rule is a strict comparison by default: a value breaches when it is strictly above 'alertAbove'/'watchAbove' or strictly below 'alertBelow'/'watchBelow'. 'alertAboveInclusive' is false by default; only the glucose 200 mg/dL review flag uses an inclusive upper bound. 'watchAboveContext' narrows a rule to one draw context. Blood pressure follows the AHA severity tiers (alert for severe hypertension, watch for stage 2). No citable general-population standard exists for mood, reaction time, consciousness or supplemental oxygen, so they carry no absolute limits. Not validated for spaceflight.

sources.label: American Heart Association - Understanding Blood Pressure Readings (Blood Pressure Categories)
American Heart Association - All About Heart Rate (resting 60-100 bpm)
American Thoracic Society - Pulse Oximetry patient sheet (cells need at least 89%; hypoxemia below 90%)
British Thoracic Society guideline for oxygen use in adults (target saturation 94-98%; significant desaturation below 90%)
Cleveland Clinic - Fever (100.4 F / 38 C oral)
AMBOSS - Fever knowledge entry (temperature above 40.0 C is a red-flag feature)
StatPearls - Vital Sign Assessment (adult respiratory rate 12-20 breaths/min)

American Diabetes Association - Diabetes Diagnosis and Tests (fasting plasma 126 mg/dL after at least 8 hours; random 200 mg/dL with symptoms; confirmation in a healthcare setting; not a universal self-diagnosis)

Joint ADA/EASD clinical-trial report: Glucose Concentrations Less Than 3 mmol/L (54 mg/dL) Should Be Reported in Clinical Trials. DOI 10.2337/dc16-2215; PMID 27872155. Clinical-trial reporting standard, not a treatment protocol.
NHLBI, NIH - How Much Sleep Is Enough (adults 7-9 hours)

systolicBloodPressure.source: American Heart Association blood pressure categories
systolicBloodPressure.basis: Severe hypertension: higher than 180 mmHg (re-measure after 1 minute per AHA). Stage 2 hypertension: 140 or higher.

labels.watchAbove: AHA stage 2 hypertension: 140 mmHg or higher

diastolicBloodPressure.source: American Heart Association blood pressure categories
diastolicBloodPressure.basis: Severe hypertension: diastolic higher than 120 mmHg. Stage 2 hypertension: 90 or higher.

labels.watchAbove: AHA stage 2 hypertension: 90 mmHg or higher

heartRate.source: American Heart Association resting heart rate
heartRate.basis: Normal adult resting heart rate is 60-100 bpm; below 60 is bradycardia, above 100 is tachycardia. Trained athletes can be lower. Extreme values are already scored by NEWS2.

labels.watchBelow: Outside AHA resting range (bradycardia): below 60 bpm
labels.watchAbove: Outside AHA resting range (tachycardia): above 100 bpm

respiratoryRate.basis: Normal adult respiratory rate is 12-20 breaths/min; tachypnea above 20, bradypnea below 12.

oxygenSaturation.source: American Thoracic Society pulse oximetry; BTS oxygen guideline
oxygenSaturation.basis: Hypoxemia is a saturation below 90%; the BTS target for most adults breathing air is 94-98%, so readings below 94% warrant attention.

temperature.basis: Fever is 38.0 C (100.4 F) oral or higher; temperature above 40.0 C is a red-flag feature.

glucose.source: American Diabetes Association diagnostic criteria; joint ADA/EASD 54 mg/dL clinical-trial report
glucose.basis: Hypoglycemia is below 70 mg/dL and clinically significant hypoglycemia below 54 mg/dL, the threshold in the joint ADA/EASD clinical-trial report (DOI 10.2337/dc16-2215, PMID 27872155; not a treatment protocol). A fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL or higher after at least 8 hours, or a random plasma glucose of 200 mg/dL or higher with hyperglycemic symptoms, is a diabetes diagnostic criterion that requires confirmation in a healthcare setting; it is not a universal self-diagnosis. The 126-199 mg/dL screening watch applies only to fasting venous plasma samples. A glucose of 200 mg/dL or higher is an editorial clinical-review flag for any context, not a validated diagnosis or triage rule. No unit conversion is applied.

labels.alertBelow: ADA significant hypoglycemia: below 54 mg/dL (joint ADA/EASD clinical-trial report)
labels.watchAbove: Fasting venous plasma glucose 126-199 mg/dL: screening watch, confirmation required
labels.alertAbove: Glucose 200 mg/dL or higher: clinical review flag, not a diagnosis

sleepHours.basis: Adults are recommended 7-9 hours a night; under 7 is associated with more health issues. Sleeping more than 9 hours is not necessarily harmful, so no upper limit is enforced.
